newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on Brazil weather worries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on Brazil weather worries.

text.p: Soybean futures on the Chicago Board of Trade ended higher Tuesday, on ideas that hot and dry weather in Brazil might damage the crop there, traders said.
"Everybody continues to watch the weather in the Southern Hemisphere," said one trader. "There is still plenty of time for problems to develop in Brazil. Their soybean crop is very young."

A late round of commission house buying also helped to push the market to end near session highs. In late trading, Prudential Securities, L.B. Stern and Cargill each bought 500,000 bushels of March, pit sources said.

However, traders with ties to Brazil reported that the crop is developing nicely despite the dry weather. Others cited weather reports showing overnight rains in Brazil's chief soybean growing regions, including Rio Grande do Sul.
Some traders said that the late surge in futures was tied to ideas that the U.S. Department of Agriculture would reduce its 1996-1997 soybean carryout in its production report on Friday.
CBOT soybeans settled up 3-1/4 to up six cents per bushel, with January up 4-1/2 at $6.98-1/2. March ended up 5-3/4 cents per bushel at $7.00-1/4.
